glosses.a22da85a32c9c575: habiendo huido en busca de refugio

notes.62ef248692ddb478: The name is spelled Judas in Spanish too.
notes.a9c3015c34f8f023: The name is spelled Israel in Spanish too.
notes.fbc35e7917672f29: STEPBible's “he sat” stands for an active plural (κατέκλιναν, “they made [them] sit”); translated by the morphology.
notes.6663a764ea548e60: STEPBible's English is garbled (“should ld be enrol”): “should be enrolled”, said of a widow.
notes.5308bf9860e69473: The English leaves the subject open, he or she; kept open.

uncertain.685fd27918df95fd: 1Cor 6:4: καθίζετε can be read as a command (“set them up!”) or a question; the sense of the verse is debated.
uncertain.6a049715d09a4d8d: John 1:5: κατέλαβεν can mean “overcame” or “comprehended”; the gloss keeps both (aprehender / apreender).
uncertain.e94eceb854aaca25: 1Cor 13:3: manuscripts differ between “be burned” and “boast”; the gloss follows one reading.
uncertain.bc3c571fbae4a2b1: Matt 16:22: ἵλεώς σοι is an idiom (literally “[God be] merciful to you”); rendered as “far be it”.
uncertain.90f3a2295df6dee0: 1Tim 5:11: καταστρηνιάω is a rare word; the exact sense (sensual desire against Christ) is uncertain.
uncertain.f6f8ee67b9a9ffec: Rom 16:7: whether the name is the woman's Junia or the man's Junias is debated; the morphology reads it feminine.
uncertain.c9983a904b57a962: 2Cor 3:18: κατοπτριζόμενοι may mean “beholding as in a mirror” or “reflecting”; debated.
